binatang.title: Cat Facts
factsarr: Cats are one of the few mammals that can't taste sweetness
Cats can jump up to 6 times their body length
Cats can dream while they sleep
Cats rarely meow at each other, only at people. With other cats they use scent, body language or sounds like growling
Cats can make more than 100 different sounds
Cats rub their heads on their owners to show affection and to mark you as part of their territory
Cats can turn their ears 180 degrees
Cats have a great sense of smell, about 14 times stronger than ours
A cat's purr makes vibrations that help bones grow and heal
Cats' bodies are made for desert life: their thick fur keeps out the heat, and their pee holds very little water so they don't waste it
Cats have a sharp sense of balance: their long tail keeps them steady as they move, and their inner ear senses changes in position and movement

binatang.title: Cool Animal Facts!
factsarr: Sea otters hold hands while they sleep so they don't drift apart
Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards
Pistol shrimp can make a sound louder than a gunshot, and heat the water to 4,400 degrees Celsius by snapping their claw shut very fast
Flamingos are born gray. Their food, brine shrimp and blue-green algae, has a natural pink color called "canthaxanthin", which turns their feathers pink
For every person, there are about 1 billion insects
The animal with the shortest life is the mayfly: an adult lives for just 24 hours
Horned lizards can squirt blood from their eyes to confuse predators
Roosters protect their own ears from their crowing by tilting their head back when they crow. This closes off the ear canal completely
Swifts can stay in the air for a whole year without ever landing
A cockroach can live for a week without its head
A blue whale's tongue can weigh as much as a car
Axolotls can regrow lost limbs up to 5 times, and even organs
An octopus has 9 brains and 3 hearts
Male seahorses get pregnant and give birth. They are the only animals where the father, not the mother, carries the babies
White-tailed jackrabbits can jump 6.4 m straight up
An ostrich's kick can kill a lion
A giant anteater can eat 35,000 ants and termites in a single day
People can smell a skunk from 5.6 km away
Only 5 percent of cheetah cubs survive to become adults
Koala fingerprints look so much like human ones that they are hard to tell apart, even under a microscope
The Dracula ant has the fastest movement of any animal: it snaps its jaws shut at up to 322 km/h in 0.000015 seconds
Pea crabs spend their whole lives inside oysters, mussels and clams
Dragonflies can't walk, even though they have six legs
A shrimp's heart is in its head. Shrimp have no arteries, so their organs float in their blood
By slowing their heartbeat, sloths can hold their breath for 40 minutes!
A blue whale's heartbeat can be heard 3 km away. Its heart weighs about 181 kg
Wild giraffes sleep only about five minutes at a time, standing up, because of the dangers around them
A grizzly bear's bite is strong enough to crush a bowling ball
To protect itself from its own powerful pecking, a woodpecker wraps its tongue around its brain
Male giraffes taste a female's pee to find out if she is ready to mate
Horses and cows can sleep standing up
The only mammal that can't jump is the elephant
Pigs can't look up at the sky
An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain
Seals are the only wild animals that can clap
Snails can sleep for up to 3 years
Spider silk is stronger than steel

binatang.title: Amphibian Facts
factsarr: Amphibians include frogs, toads, salamanders and newts
Amphibians can breathe and soak up water through their very thin skin
Amphibians need water or a damp place to survive
The longest-living amphibian is the giant salamander
The biggest amphibian is the giant salamander, which grows to 1.4 meters long
The smallest amphibian is the Paedophryne amauensis frog from New Guinea, just 7.7 mm long
The most colorful amphibians are the most poisonous: their colors warn predators
Almost all amphibians go through metamorphosis, changing shape from egg to larva to adult. As larvae they live in water; once they grow legs and lungs, they become adults and live on land
They are cold-blooded, which means their body temperature changes with their surroundings
Because of their special skin they need very particular living conditions: too much sun can damage their cells, and too much wind can dry out their skin and dehydrate them

binatang.title: Fish Facts
factsarr: Fish breathe with gills. When a fish opens its mouth, water flows over the gills and the blood in tiny vessels takes in the oxygen dissolved in the water
The biggest fish in the world is the whale shark, which can be 10 meters long and weigh about 15,000 kg
The smallest fish in the world is Paedocypris progenetica, found in Sumatra! It is only about 7.9 mm long
Most fish see more colors than people do; they are tetrachromats
Fish are among the oldest animals in the world. They were around long before the dinosaurs
Fish are cold-blooded, so their body temperature depends on their surroundings
The deepest fish ever found is the snailfish, seen 8,336 meters down
Some fish, like sharks and catfish, track their prey by sensing electrical signals in the water
Fish can breathe in water because most of the ocean's oxygen is made by plankton, floating plants, algae and some bacteria
There are 2 kinds of fish: those that live in salt water, like the ocean sunfish, and those that live in fresh water, like the pike

binatang.title: Reptile Facts
factsarr: Reptiles have special skin made of scales, bony plates or both
Every reptile regularly sheds the outer layer of its skin
They are cold-blooded, so their temperature depends on their surroundings
With no fur to keep them warm and no sweat glands to cool down, they move into the sun when it's cold and into the shade when it's hot
Boas and pythons are famous snakes, but only boas give birth to live young; pythons and most other reptiles lay eggs in nests
For some reptiles, whether a baby is male or female depends on the temperature of the egg as it develops
The biggest reptile is the saltwater crocodile. The komodo dragon is the biggest lizard, but not the biggest reptile
The smallest reptile is the nano-chameleon, about the size of a sunflower seed
Many reptiles don't chew their food but swallow it whole, so they digest it slowly
Some turtles take in oxygen from the water through their bottoms while they hibernate

binatang.title: Bird Facts
factsarr: Flamingos can only eat with their heads upside down
Ostriches lay the biggest eggs, which can weigh up to 1.5 kilograms
The smallest bird in the world is the hummingbird, and it lays the smallest eggs, about the size of a pea
A bird's heart can beat up to 1,200 times a minute while flying, depending on the kind of bird and the temperature
There is a poisonous bird in Papua New Guinea, the pitohui. Its poison is in its skin and feathers
The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird in the world, reaching 389 km/h in a dive. The fastest in level flight is the common swift, at 169 km/h
Albatrosses can sleep while flying, usually gliding at about 40 km/h
Owls can't move their eyes, but they can turn their heads 270 degrees
Woodpeckers can peck 20 times a second

binatang.title: Dog Facts
factsarr: A dog's nose print is unique, just like a human fingerprint
Dogs can dream, especially puppies and old dogs
A dog's nose has 300 million scent receptors; a person has about 5 million
A dog's nose can sense heat, so even blind or deaf dogs can still hunt
A person yawning can make a dog yawn too! It's 4 times more likely if the dog knows that person
Dogs curl up when they sleep to protect their organs from predators, a habit from their wild ancestors
A dog's blood pressure goes down when you pet it
Dogs mostly see the colors yellow and blue
Dalmatians are born white; their black spots appear as they grow
Dogs have about 1,700 taste buds; people have between 2,000 and 10,000
Dogs kick backwards after going to the toilet to mark their territory with scent glands in their feet
Studies show that dogs are among the few animals that are kind to others without expecting anything back

binatang.title: Animals of Indonesia
factsarr: Komodo dragon - They are venomous! They eat almost any kind of meat, from small rodents to big water buffalo. Their young mostly eat small lizards, insects, snakes and birds
Maleo - When a maleo egg hatches underground, the chick has to dig its way up to the surface, which can be a whole meter. They eat nuts, fruit, seeds, snails, insects and other invertebrates.
Celebes crested macaque - They are found only in Minahasa on Sulawesi island and around Bacan island. They eat fruit and live in groups of 5-25 monkeys, sometimes up to 75!
Sumatran tiger - Fewer than 600 Sumatran tigers are left in the wild. They usually hunt wild boar and deer, but will hunt other prey when they can
Javan rhino - There are only about 76 in the world. They eat only plants and live alone, except when pairing up or caring for their young
Pygmy tarsier - They eat only arthropods like spiders, beetles, termites, ants and caterpillars. They have huge eyes
Bornean elephant - They are smaller than other elephants. They eat roots, grass, leaves, bananas and sugar cane.
Sumatran orangutan - They live in the trees almost all their lives. Females never come down, and males very rarely do. They mostly eat fruit, insects and sometimes bird eggs or small animals.
Bali myna - They eat insects and sometimes worms, small reptiles and fruit.
Javan gibbon - Their long arms and fingers help them swing between branches. They are omnivores that eat fruit, leaves and sometimes nectar and grubs
White cockatoo - They usually build nests in holes in very big, tall trees. They eat nuts, seeds and fruits like durian, rambutan, papaya and langsat. While nesting they also eat insects.

Bald bird-of-paradise - Males dance to win over females. Before starting, a male clears the ground of leaves and anything else that could get in the way of his dance. They mostly eat fruit and a few small insects.
Anoa - They live alone or in pairs. They are hard to spot because they often hide. They mostly eat grass, leaves and fruit.

Babirusa - Their tusks grow right through the skin of the snout and curve back toward the forehead. In males the tusks never stop growing and can break when they fight other males. They eat leaves, fruit, nuts, mushrooms, bark, insects, fish and small mammals!

Sunda clouded leopard - They are active at night, live alone and guard their territory. Males usually have bigger territories than females. They are meat eaters and eat rodents, beetles, lizards, snakes, frogs, geckos and small birds.

binatang.title: Mammal Facts
factsarr: They are covered in hair or fur
They are warm-blooded, which means their body temperature stays the same whatever the weather outside
Most grow inside their mother's womb before birth, for between 13 and 210 days
After birth, babies drink milk made by their mother's mammary glands
Their brains are bigger and more complex than those of other animals
Most of them have good hearing
A few mammals lay eggs. They are called monotremes, like the platypus and echidnas
They are heterodonts, which means they have different kinds of teeth

binatang.title: Invertebrate Facts
factsarr: Invertebrates are animals with no backbone or bony skeleton

There are 6 main groups of invertebrates: arthropods (insects, spiders and crustaceans like crabs), cnidarians (jellyfish, coral, sea anemones), echinoderms (starfish, sea cucumbers, sea urchins), mollusks (snails, squid, octopus), segmented worms (earthworms, leeches) and sponges
Invertebrates are the biggest group in the animal world, about 97 percent of all animals. Most invertebrates are insects

Insects are the most successful invertebrates because they adapt easily. They can eat animals, plants and rotting matter, live in very hot and dry places, and fly to escape predators or find food, water and new homes
The biggest invertebrate is the giant squid
The smallest invertebrates are myxozoans, parasites only a few micrometers long as adults

angkasa.title: Sun Facts
factsarr: The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old
The inside of the Sun reaches 15 million °C
Sometimes gas on the Sun's surface bursts out and spreads far into space. These are called solar flares, and they can disturb satellites and stop phones, TVs and other electronics from working
Sunlight takes 8 minutes to reach Earth
Every planet in the Solar System orbits the Sun
The Sun is made of 74% hydrogen and 24% helium, so it is made only of gas
Without the Sun, animals, people and plants couldn't live. Earth would be far too cold, and plants need sunlight to make their food
A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun
More than a million Earths could fit inside the Sun
The Sun's gravity keeps our planet moving around the Solar System
One day the Sun will run out of its fuel, hydrogen, and go out. But that won't happen for another 5 billion years

angkasa.title: Earth Facts
factsarr: Earth is the third planet from the Sun in our Solar System
Earth is about 4.5 billion years old
Earth's air is 78 percent nitrogen, 21 percent oxygen and 1 percent other gases. That's just right for life
Earth doesn't have rings like some other planets
Earth's atmosphere protects us from incoming meteoroids; most of them break up before they reach the ground
Earth is a terrestrial planet, which means it is made mostly of rock
It is the only planet in the Solar System known to support life
Earth is the only planet with exactly one moon

angkasa.title: Milky Way Facts
factsarr: The Milky Way is a galaxy. A galaxy is a huge group of stars (like the Sun) and planets gathered together in space
The Milky Way holds hundreds of billions of stars like our Sun, and most stars have at least one planet orbiting them
Earth sits about halfway between the center of the Milky Way and its outer edge
The Andromeda galaxy is the closest big galaxy to the Milky Way, about two and a half million light-years away (a light-year is how far light travels in one Earth year)
The Milky Way is 13.6 billion years old
Earth is 26,000 light-years from the center of the Milky Way
On a clear night you can see part of the Milky Way from Earth.
The Milky Way is 10-15% dust and gas; the rest is stars
There is a black hole at the center of the Milky Way
Scientists think the Milky Way is 13.6 billion years old, almost as old as the universe, which is 13.8 billion years old

angkasa.title: Comet Facts
factsarr: Comets are big lumps of dust and ice that orbit the Sun
They are leftovers from when our Solar System formed
Some comets come from the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune's orbit, and others from an even farther region called the Oort Cloud
When a comet gets close to the Sun, ice and dust boil off its frozen center, called the nucleus, and form a cloud called the coma. Sunlight blows gas and dust from the coma into a beautiful tail

angkasa.title: Venus Facts
factsarr: Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System, with a surface temperature of 462 °C. Its thick atmosphere traps heat and makes it very hot
Venus is the second closest planet to the Sun
Venus is a terrestrial planet, which means it is made of rock
A day on Venus lasts 243 Earth days, and a year lasts 225 Earth days. So on Venus, a year is shorter than a day!
With today's technology, it would take about 6 months to travel to Venus
Venus is only a little smaller than Earth
Gravity on Venus is 91% of Earth's. So if you weigh 100 kg on Earth, you would weigh only 91 kg on Venus
Venus has more volcanoes than any other planet in the Solar System, though most are asleep

angkasa.title: Saturn Facts
factsarr: Saturn is a gas giant like Jupiter. It is made mostly of hydrogen and helium
Saturn has seven main rings with gaps between them. They are made of chunks of ice and rock
A day on Saturn is 10.7 hours. A year on Saturn is 29 Earth years
As of June 8, 2023, Saturn had 146 known moons.
Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun, after Jupiter and before Uranus
The temperature at Saturn's cloud tops is about -178 °C.
With today's technology, it would take about 3 years to travel to Saturn
If you weigh 100 kg on Earth, you would weigh 107 kg on Saturn

angkasa.title: Neptune Facts
factsarr: Neptune is dark, cold and very windy
Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun in the Solar System, beyond Uranus. It is about 30 times farther from the Sun than Earth is
Neptune has six rings that are very hard to see
Neptune, like Uranus, is an ice giant. It is made of a thick soup of water, ammonia and methane flowing over a solid core about the size of Earth
Neptune has a thick, windy atmosphere
A day on Neptune is 16 hours. A year on Neptune is 165 Earth years
The temperature at Neptune's cloud tops is about -214 °C
With today's technology, it would take about 12 years to travel to Neptune
If you weigh 100 kg on Earth, you would weigh 114 kg on Neptune

angkasa.title: Mercury Facts
factsarr: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun
It is the second hottest planet in the Solar System
It is the smallest planet in the Solar System
It is a rocky planet like Earth, with a surface that looks like the Moon's
A day on Mercury lasts 59 Earth days
A year on Mercury is just 88 Earth days: it is so close to the Sun that its orbit is short
Mercury is named after the Roman god who carried messages for the other gods
Even though it is so close to the Sun, Mercury has ice, because some parts get almost no direct sunlight and stay dark
Gravity on Mercury is only 38% of Earth's. So if you weigh 100 kg on Earth, you would weigh only 38 kg on Mercury
With today's technology, it would take about 4 years to travel to Mercury
Mercury's surface can reach 117 °C on average, and much hotter in the daytime

angkasa.title: Pluto Facts
factsarr: Pluto is a dwarf planet, which means it is smaller than the other planets
Pluto was called a planet until 2006
Pluto is usually farther away than Neptune, but because its orbit is an oval, it is sometimes closer to the Sun than Neptune
Pluto is smaller than Earth's Moon
A day on Pluto is 153 hours. A year on Pluto is 248 Earth years
Pluto's surface temperature is about -228 °C to -238 °C
Pluto has mountains with white peaks made of frozen methane

angkasa.title: Jupiter Facts
factsarr: Jupiter is the biggest planet in the Solar System. It is more than twice as heavy as all the other planets put together
Jupiter has a giant storm called the "Great Red Spot" that has lasted for hundreds of years
Jupiter is a gas giant with no solid surface. It is made mostly of hydrogen and helium
Jupiter has rings that are very hard to see
Jupiter has a very thick atmosphere
A day on Jupiter is 10 hours. A year on Jupiter is 11.8 Earth years
Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun, after Mars and before Saturn
The temperature at Jupiter's cloud tops is about -148 °C
With today's technology, it would take about 13 months to travel to Jupiter
If you weigh 100 kg on Earth, you would weigh 253 kg on Jupiter

angkasa.title: Asteroid Facts
factsarr: Asteroids are leftovers from when the Solar System formed about 4.6 billion years ago, and they orbit the Sun in ovals
Some asteroids have their own moons
Most asteroids orbit the Sun in the Asteroid Belt, but sometimes Jupiter's gravity pulls one out of the belt and sends it toward Earth. A piece that lands on Earth is called a meteorite
There are millions of asteroids in the Solar System
Some asteroids become moons: a planet's gravity pulls them in and they start orbiting it
Asteroids can even have rings: streams of dust that circle around them
Asteroids are rich in carbon, silica and metals. Some have water ice trapped inside their rubble

angkasa.title: Mars Facts
factsarr: Mars is named after the Roman god of war
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun in the Solar System
Mars is red because of a lot of iron oxide, or 'rust', in its rocks and soil
Mars is the second smallest planet in the Solar System after Mercury. It is about half the size of Earth
The temperature on Mars ranges from 20 °C at the equator to -140 °C at the poles
Mars has the tallest mountain in the Solar System, a volcano called Olympus Mons. It is 24 kilometers high, about 3 times taller than Mount Everest
Because gravity on Mars is weaker than on Earth, you could jump 3 times higher there
A day on Mars is 24 hours and 37 minutes. But a year on Mars is 687 days, because Mars takes longer to go around the Sun
In 2018, scientists found signs of a lake under the ice at Mars's south pole
Mars has 2 moons, Phobos and Deimos
With today's technology, it would take about 7-8 months to travel to Mars

angkasa.title: Black Hole Facts
factsarr: A black hole is a place in space where gravity pulls so hard that not even light can escape
Its gravity is so strong because a lot of matter is squeezed into a very small space. This can happen when a star is dying
Because no light can escape, we can't see black holes. They are invisible
Space telescopes with special tools can help find black holes, by spotting how stars very close to a black hole move differently from other stars
A black hole as small as an atom can have the mass of a big mountain: it holds as much matter as a mountain does
The biggest black holes are called "supermassive". They have more mass than 1 million Suns put together. Every big galaxy has a supermassive black hole at its center
Scientists think the smallest black holes formed when the universe began, and that supermassive black holes formed at the same time as the galaxies they are in
There are probably millions of black holes in our galaxy that we will never find
If you fell into a black hole, you could never get out

angkasa.title: Uranus Facts
factsarr: Uranus is circled by 13 rings. The inner rings are narrow and dark; the outer rings are bright and easier to see
Uranus is an ice giant. It is made mostly of water, methane and ammonia fluids above a small rocky center
Uranus has a thick atmosphere of methane, hydrogen and helium
Uranus is the only planet that spins on its side
A day on Uranus is 17 hours and 14 minutes. A year on Uranus is 84 Earth years
Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun, after Saturn and before Neptune
The temperature at Uranus's cloud tops is about -216 °C
With today's technology, it would take about 9 years to travel to Uranus
If you weigh 100 kg on Earth, you would weigh 91 kg on Uranus

factsarr: Horses and cows can sleep standing up

Women's hearts beat faster than men's, on average about 7-8 more beats per minute

An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain

Twelve percent of people dream only in black and white

The human brain is about 80% water
About two thousand different languages are spoken in Africa
People can't walk in a straight line with their eyes closed
Your brain hides your nose, so you usually don't see it
The human body contains about 0.2 milligrams of gold, mostly in our blood.
Peanut butter can be turned into diamonds with a scientific process

aneh.title: 20 Weird Facts Part 1
factsarr: Before alarm clocks, people paid someone to tap on their window to wake them up. They were called knocker-uppers.
Arithmophobia is the fear of numbers.
You spend about a third of your life asleep
The Eiffel Tower grows up to 15 centimeters taller in summer because metal expands in the heat
Switzerland bans keeping just one guinea pig or parrot, because they are social animals and a single one would get very lonely
A shrimp's heart is in its head. Shrimp have no arteries, so their organs float in their blood
By slowing their heartbeat, sloths can hold their breath for 40 minutes!
A blue whale's heartbeat can be heard 3 km away. Its heart weighs about 181 kg
A cloud can weigh about 453,592 kg
Wild giraffes sleep only about five minutes at a time, standing up, because of the dangers around them
Clownfish can change from male to female once in their lives
A grizzly bear's bite is strong enough to crush a bowling ball
To protect itself from its own powerful pecking, a woodpecker wraps its tongue around its brain
Male giraffes taste a female's pee to find out if she is ready to mate
